name: FormNexa MultiStep Forms
author: Amigo Dheena

sections.description:
Create forms in FormNexa Forms, add steps and fields, then publish. Paste the shortcode shown in the dashboard into a post or page, or use the FormNexa Form block with the form ID.

Use [formnexa_multistep_form id="123"] to embed a published form, replacing 123 with its form ID.

The editable source for every shipped asset is included in this plugin. blocks/block.js is the readable block source loaded directly by WordPress. public/form.js and public/form.css are the sources for public/form.min.js and public/form.min.css; admin/admin.css is the source for admin/admin.min.css. admin/admin.js is also shipped as readable source. No third-party JavaScript or CSS libraries are bundled.

For checkbox, radio, and icon-card options, each option starts without an image. In Field settings > Options, optionally upload an SVG or PNG image for each option. Set Image size (px) on the field to control the image size in the builder and the published form. SVG images are limited to 100 KB and PNG images to 300 KB and 1024 × 1024 pixels. Uploaded images are stored with that form’s configuration.

Submission records are stored in dedicated WordPress tables. Form admins can view entries at FormNexa Forms > Entries and export a form’s entries as CSV. Each new entry emails the address configured in the form’s Actions tab; when that field is blank, it uses the WordPress site administrator email. Configure the built-in transport at FormNexa Forms > SMTP Settings with the host, port, encryption, sender, and optional login supplied by your email provider. Save, then send a test email from that page. The Entries list shows whether WordPress accepted the message or reported a failure. The SMTP password is stored in the WordPress database, or it can be supplied through the FORMNEXA_FORMS_SMTP_PASSWORD constant in wp-config.php. Uploaded files are kept in entry records and can only be downloaded by administrators.

Deactivating the plugin keeps forms and entries. Deleting it through WordPress removes its forms, entries, SMTP settings, and temporary submission records, including on sites in a Multisite network.

Administrator submission emails use a navy and blue HTML template with a plain-text alternative. Selected checkbox, radio, and icon-card SVG/PNG option images are embedded inline; their text labels remain visible when a mail client blocks images. Each answer is escaped before display, and private file-upload contents are never included in email.

Privacy

Form submissions, including any uploaded files, are stored in this site’s WordPress database. Notification emails send submitted answers to the form’s configured recipient, or to the site administrator when no recipient is configured. Uploaded file contents are not included in notification emails. If SMTP is enabled, the configured mail provider handles those emails. The plugin does not set an automatic retention period or provide a personal-data exporter or eraser. Entries remain until the plugin is deleted through WordPress or a site administrator removes them directly from the database. Site administrators should account for submissions and notification emails in their privacy policy and respond to privacy requests according to that policy.

1.0.0

  • Initial release with multi-step form building, entries, email notifications, and SMTP settings.
